output.summary: The record year is mostly a commodity-price effect, not an Operational Excellence effect. Revenue rose 46.5% while bushels fell 0.9%, and the auditor ties the merchandising gain to the Feb-June 2026 price rally. Peers without any improvement program grew net savings faster (median +97% vs Cottonwood's 10th-of-23 rank). The 6% cost-per-bushel gain comes almost entirely from maintenance spending falling, while deferred work orders tripled and Harlan Junction has an open dust and bearing hazard with an insurer deadline of 21 Nov. The drying and grading know-how sits with one near-retirement superintendent with no successor. The expansion case is built on inflated FY2026 revenue with no margin or debt-service analysis. Defer the vote, fix the hazards now, and start succession now. Do not hold maintenance flat.
